messages:
maria: heads up — we found a medium CVE chain in one of our base layers (openssl deps). planning a base-image rebuild + re-sign + deploy. need to coordinate RBAC, KMS key use, and audit logging before we push canaries.
jonathan: do we have an estimate for blast radius? which images use that base?
maria: scanning shows ~18 internal images and 4 customer-facing images. impact is mostly runtime containers, not build-time tools.
kevin: if we're re-signing, we should avoid reusing the main signing key — propose a short-lived per-rebuild key wrapped by KMS so we can revoke fast if something goes wrong.
alex: agree. also we need to ensure the canary fleet uses the exact signed digest (not :latest). add a rollout window for low-traffic hours.
sam: question on audit: which events do we need to log for compliance? signing, key-wrap ops, and image admission decisions?
maria: yes — signing ops + key unwrap/wrap + cosign verification events + admission controller decisions. retention 365 days for prod.
sec-bot: [scan-report] image: base/ubuntu-20.04:cv-2026-xyz found libs with CVSS 6.1 — flagged at 2026-03-20T14:02Z :warning:
jonathan: can we do build-time mitigations (patching libs) vs full rebase?
maria: patching likely ok for some layers but we still want a rebuild to normalize SBOMs and attestations. rebase recommended for long term.
kevin: RBAC items: build runners currently have broad iam:encrypt/decrypt on /kms/main-signing-key. we should scope to a new role roles/image-writer with kms:EncryptOnly and cosign signer IAM. Then a separate roles/image-signer with kms:AsymmetricSign for the short-lived rebase key.
lina: tiny nit — CI needs permission to upload to artifact registry and to create attestations. recommend 'artifactregistry.packageWriter' + 'binaryauthorization.attestorAdmin' for canary job principal.
alex: runbook step suggestion: 1) create short-lived signing key (key-id: rebuild-2026-03-20) 2) scope RBAC to roles/image-signer on that key 3) rebuild images in staging 4) sign with cosign using KMS key 5) run canaries 6) promote and rotate main key.
jonathan: can we get a sample cosign command for signing with cloud KMS? saves time.
kevin: sure — example for GCP KMS asymmetric key:```
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign-blob --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/image-keys/cryptoKeys/rebuild-2026 --output-signature rebuild.sig ./image.tar
```
maria: also add verification step to admission controller: verify signature is by key-id rebuild-2026 or main-key before allowing run. reject unsigned.
sam: audit logs need to capture: kms.keyAccess, cosign.signerIdentity, artifact push, admission verdict. Let's map those to SIEM fields we already index.
kevin: note: cloud KMS asymmetric signing will emit keyRingAccess logs to audit-logs. we need to ensure log export to sec-logs is enabled and retention policy set to 1y. config snippet:```
resource("logging_project_sink") {
  destination = "bigquery://sec-logs.ds.logs"
  filter = "resource.type=\"k8s_container\" OR protoPayload.methodName:DecryptKey OR protoPayload.methodName:SignBlob"
}
```
lina: who owns the artifact registry permissions change?
jonathan: I can do the CI changes (rebuild pipeline and attestation upload). need a ticket and RBAC PR.
maria: kevin can you create the temporary KMS key and the IAM roles? include a small doc with who gets which role and TTL for key.
kevin: yes. will provision 'rebuild-2026-03-20' asymmetric key with 48h TTL and role bindings for jonathan-ci and canary-sa. I'll open a PR in infra-iam.
sec-bot: [vuln-triage] assigned to @maria, @jonathan — please ack in 2h or escalate to pager.
maria: acked. I'll start coordination with oncall to schedule the canary at 02:00 UTC.
alex: on incident/rollback plan: if canary fails integrity checks or we see increased 5xx, we should 1) unroute canaries 2) mark image immutable and roll back to previous digest, 3) revoke rebuild key, 4) trigger postmortem. Add runbook links.
maria: adding a short checklist to the thread: [ ] KMS key created + IAM PR merged, [ ] CI pipeline updated + test artifacts pushed, [ ] SBOM & attestations generated, [ ] Staging canary pass, [ ] Prod canary window scheduled, [ ] Audit export validated.
jonathan: I'll open a GH issue with that checklist and attach the build logs.
kevin: infra-iam PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3194 (WIP) — bindings for roles/image-signer.
lina: pinging legal for retention confirmation: @legal-security — is 365d OK for KMS and image-signing logs?
sam: legal confirmed offline — 365 days is acceptable for this case, need to capture justification in ticket.
maria: final Q: any objections to rolling in 48h window with a single prod canary group (5% traffic) then 24h monitor?
alex: :+1: from SRE. ensure alert for anomaly detection uses token-level latencies and error-rate SLOs.
jonathan: starting rebuild job now in staging. will paste logs here when ready.
sec-bot: [build-notify] staging-rebuild-2026-03-20 completed — image digests: sha256:aaa111... :white_check_mark:
jonathan: staging signed and attested. verification snippet:```
cosign verify --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/.../cryptoKeys/rebuild-2026 gcr.io/redwood/base@sha256:aaa111
```
maria: thanks. I'll schedule the canary and post a final runbook link. last action: kevin to merge infra-iam PR, jonathan to queue prod pipeline, alex to watch canary.
kevin: PR merged. key rotated to disabled on expiry schedule.
jonathan: prod canary queued for 2026-03-22T02:00Z.
lina: created ticket RW-5421 with checklist and links.
maria: closing loop — if canary looks good after 24h we'll promote. otherwise rollback and follow incident runbook. thanks team :lock:
